title: RAW Galen II.8: beneficial heat versus fever as a causal counterargument
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Preserve a connected argument in which an injury precedes fever but impaired digestion appears with fever; more of a proposed helpful influence cannot alone explain the impairment.

source.unit: II.8 bounded complete argument from the wound/bubo example through the conclusion that abnormal heat impairs human gastric activity, printedpp185-189.
source.checked: Full selected paragraph argument read in the institutional English witness; its ancient physiology is reported, not endorsed.
source.content: A wound/bubo precedes digestive impairment, which begins with fever. Galen challenges an account relying on stronger pneuma-driven activity and argues that excessive heat explains the failure.

design.whole_passage_relation: The complete account retains before/after observations, rival mechanism, implication of increased activity, contradiction with observed failure, and the alternative cause.
two_reused_input_cases: Same patient with wound but before fever: alleged direct injury cause lacks the predicted digestive effect.
Same patient after fever: impaired digestion coexists with increased activity that the rival calls helpful.
design.rival: Monotonic MORE_HEAT/MORE_ACTIVITY produces better digestion; the injury directly blocks the stomach.
design.distinct_consequence: A threshold or disproportion relation differs from a global positive modifier; unchanged injury cannot alone explain changed outcome under the stated temporal observations.
design.falsifier: Fail if the complete target reading needs to turn one stable modifier into beneficial and harmful senses without an explicit excess/context distinction, or loses patient/event identity.
design.smallest_step: Author the entire argument with two time slices and explicit quoted-rival versus narrator assertions; retain which conclusion belongs to which speaker.
new_costs: One temporal comparison and one attribution construction.
Do not infer numerical optimum, clinical truth or a modern causal experiment.
